column1: # registry-catalog.tsv — META-CATALOG: a REGISTRY OF REGISTRIES (KS29 primitive applied
# recursively; Backstage software-catalog pattern). REGISTRY-META-CATALOG ticket, 2026-07-24.
# HARD OPERATOR CONSTRAINT — INDEX, NOT CONTAINER:
#   This file lists the registries THEMSELVES, never their contents. Each registry's data
#   stays in its own file. This file grows with the NUMBER of registries (~a dozen), NEVER
#   with their entries — so it CANNOT become a god-file, and editing a registry's DATA never
#   touches this file. fleet/tests/registry-catalog.test.sh asserts NO data-value column
#   (anti-god-file guard) and that no catalogued registry's data value leaks in here.
# SCHEMA (exactly 6 metadata/pointer columns — no data-value column, structurally):
#   name             short id of the registry
#   purpose          one-line what-it-is
#   path             repo-root-relative pointer to the registry file (NOT its contents)
#   schema           the registry's OWN column list (metadata about its shape, not its data)
#   owner            ticket/component that owns the registry
#   conformance_gate the check that keeps that registry honest (or '-' if none yet)
# AUTO-DISCOVERY (fail-closed): fleet/checks/discover-registries.sh scans the tree for
# registry files by convention (*-registry.tsv, *-register.tsv, *-pool.{txt,tsv},
# case-insensitive) and reconciles them against this index. A convention-named registry on
# disk but ABSENT here -> the discovery leg FAILS CLOSED (exit non-zero). Non-convention
# registries (e.g. tier-models.tsv) are seeded here so they are findable; extra rows are fine.
# name
